deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.content: # DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See [Web UI guide](docs/user/guide/index.md). ### Run from source To run from a repository checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git cd deepseek-harness pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dsh web ``` `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. ## Community and support - Submit feedback or bug reports through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions). - Add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic to your plugin repository for discoverability. - Join DeepSeek Harness Discord community. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). `pnpm run dev:web` builds, serves, and rebuilds client bundles on source edits in one terminal, and `make help` lists the matching Make targets for Web and Desktop; the guide's application commands section owns the full table. For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseek-harness2026, title={DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, publisher={GitHub}, howpublished={\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness}}, } ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

A small LLM writes text only when the operation is `TYPE_TEXT`. **Zürich → London on Google Flights in 7.1 seconds.** One natural-language goal, actual text generation, and loading waits included. [Watch the MP4](docs/demo.mp4) · [Measurements](docs/performance.md) · [Read the loop](jev_ultrafast/agent.py) ## The action space Every observation produces a new element table: ```text [1] button Change ticket type · Round trip [2] combobox Where from? · San Francisco [3] combobox Where to? · empty [4] textbox Departure · empty ... ``` The operations are `CLICK`, `TYPE_TEXT`, `SELECT`, `SCROLL_UP`, `SCROLL_DOWN`, `WAIT`, `DONE`, and `BLOCKED`. Only supported operations and targets are offered. ```text one TypeSafe request ┌───────────────────────────┐ page → element table → operation │ │ click_target │ │ type_text_target │ │ select_target, if present │ └─────────────┬─────────────┘ use the matching target │ CLICK [7] ─────┤──→ browser TYPE_TEXT [3] ─────┘ ↓ small LLM → text → browser ``` Target questions are speculative. If the operation is `CLICK`, only `click_target` can execute. Two decisions, **one network round trip**. Each target head contains only compatible elements. robbietilton/Compositor.content:
# Compositor

Adobe Photoshop costs too much and tools like GIMP don’t feel familiar enough for me to stay in flow. That’s why I built Compositor.

The goal was to create a full-featured image editor that is completely free and open source. I used to use Photoshop for compositing and post-processing, so Compositor is built around that workflow - with the tools needed to create a pixel-perfect final image.

Because it’s open source, you can download the Xcode project and add, remove, or modify any feature to fit your workflow.

## Installation

### Download
Get Compositor from [robbietilton.com/compositor](https://robbietilton.com/compositor), or download the latest release directly from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/robbietilton/Compositor/releases/latest).

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install --cask robbietilton-compositor
```

## Features

### Layers
- Layers and folders, with opacity and Photoshop's full set of blend modes in its order — a folder's opacity dims everything inside it
- Layer masks: paint, fill, invert, blur and feather them anywhere on the canvas, past the layer's own pixels; link or unlink them to transform a mask on its own
- Clipping masks and folder masks
- Adjustment layers: Hue/Saturation, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Gradient Map, Grain, Black & White, Color Balance, Invert, and filter layers: Gaussian Blur, Motion Blur, Progressive Blur, Sharpen, Reduce Noise, Noise, Vignette, Bloom / Glow, RGB Split, Lens Effects and Tonal Contrast
- Layer effects: Stroke, Drop Shadow, Color Overlay, Inner Shadow, Outer Glow and Inner Glow, rendered on the GPU and editable at any time
- Merge Down, Merge Layers and Merge Group (⌘E)
- Duplicate, rename inline, reorder and nest by drag and drop; Option-drag to duplicate; a right-click menu in the Layers panel
- Copy and paste whole layers and folders (⌘C/⌘V with no selection), within a project or between projects, or drag them between projects

### Transform
- Non-destructive move, scale, rotate and flip — images keep their full resolution however small you make them
- Free distort (⌘-drag a handle), with Shift to lock to an axis
- Transform several layers, or a whole folder, together
- Snapping to canvas and layer edges and centers, with guides
- Distances (View › Show › Distances): pixel gaps to the canvas edges and nearby layers while moving a layer, and to the layer under the pointer with ⌘ held
- Exact values for position, size, scale and angle, stepped with the arrow keys
- Flip Layer and Flip Canvas, horizontal and vertical
- Align and Distribute layers to each other, the selection or the canvas, from the Move tool's bar or the Layer menu

### Selections
- Rectangle and Ellipse Marquee, Freehand and Polygonal Lasso, and the Magic tool — Wand selects by color, Object traces whatever you click (Tab switches)
- Select Subject, and Expand, Contract and Feather on any selection
- Add to and subtract from selections, move the outline, or move and duplicate the pixels inside

NandhaKishorM/laya.content:
laya is free and open source. If it helps you, sponsor the work on GitHub.

**New in 0.5: laya reads images, audio and video, takes 73k tokens, says when it should not decide, and keeps learning.** All open source under Apache 2.0 (`pip install -U laya`). - **Text, images, audio and video.** `agent.predict(...)` with `image=`, `audio=` or `video=` gives the same typed answers as for text. - **73,728 tokens of context.** Whole contracts, threads and logs in one read. - **Abstain and unbound**, explained below. - **Physics, not text generation.** Each candidate answer is a valley; the input is a particle that rolls and settles in one. Deterministic, constant cost, nothing generated. - **Any LLM as the reader.** One small decision engine on top of a frozen reader, from 0.8B to 27B. - **Continuous learning.** `from laya import Learner`: it answers from day one and learns from every answer your team confirms, on your own machine, in seconds on a CPU with no fine-tuning. - **A teacher for what it is unsure of.** `laya.Escalator(learner, teacher)` sends only the records it abstains on, finds unbound or is not yet sure of to your teacher (a review queue, a rules engine, or a model you serve yourself with `laya.vllm_teacher`), serves that answer and learns from it, so the teacher is needed less and less. [Guide](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/docs/vegaml.md#a-teacher-for-what-it-is-unsure-of). ### How abstain and unbound work The input is placed as a particle in a small decision space where every candidate answer is a valley. Where the particle settles, and how deep, is the answer and its probability. - **`abstain`**: it declines to commit. The threshold is calibrated so that, among the answers it does give, the error rate stays under the configured risk (10% by default). - **`prediction_set`**: the conformal set, every option the answer could still be at `alpha` 0.10. One option means it is sure; two or more means the input really is ambiguous. - **`unbound`**: the particle settled far from every v…

# Readme

This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an unnamed internal OpenAI model. 

As part of model development, we evaluate our models on open research problems. We expanded these evaluations after performance on our existing mathematical evaluations saturated. Some outputs build upon earlier results produced by the models.

This collection includes results at different stages of verification. Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations. We will continue to update this repository with Lean formalizations as we obtain them. 

Some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly.
We are also exploring community-hosted repositories for these materials. 

In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data, rather than polished academic papers. We defer to the math community completely on matters of credit, precedence, and concurrent work.

## Navigating the collection

The current catalogue contains 721 manuscripts organized into 373 families. A family groups related papers, which may include a principal result, companion arguments, consequences, or alternative proofs. Each family is classified by mathematical discipline.

- Start with the [overview](overview.pdf) for descriptions of the families.
- Use the [manuscript map](CONTENTS.md) to find individual papers and their supporting materials.
- The [`preprints/`](preprints/) directory contains PDFs, source files, and manuscript-specific citation and build instructions.
- The [Lean library](lean/README.md) and [formalization catalogue](lean/formalization.yaml) describe the available formal proofs, their associated papers, and verification configurations. See the [Comparator instructions](lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md) for additional checking instructions. The repository has ~42% top-line results formalized.
- Updates to the repo are described in the [history](history.md).

### Reasoning summaries

We are also releasing abridged summaries of the model's reasoning, covering the following results:

|---|---|

# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

### Prerequisites

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

google-research/harness2.content:
Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the task-level recursion budget brings further gains. The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**. ## Video overview https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f…

NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for

# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, install it as a plugin. Run this in a terminal to get it in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install unslop --marketplace heydamir/unslop
```

On an older Claude Code without `--marketplace`, the same in two steps:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir
```

To get it in a single project only, run the install from that project's root folder, the one you start Claude Code in, and add `--scope local`. To turn it on for everyone who works in the project, add `--scope project` instead and commit `.claude/settings.json`. Each teammate then runs this once in their own copy of the project:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir --scope project
```

Then start a new Claude Code session, or run `/reload-plugins` in one that is already open.

To update, run `claude plugin update unslop@heydamir`, or turn on auto-update for the heydamir marketplace under Marketplaces in `/plugin`.

If you copied unslop into `~/.claude/skills/` or a project's `.claude/skills/` before, delete that copy, or `/unslop` keeps running it instead of the plugin.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/config/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available…

# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

# Claude animation skills

Skills for Claude Code that make animations for reels, with no footage needed. You type `/map-route home to the gym, 2.8 km` and Claude writes the spec, renders the animation on your own computer and checks it against Instagram's safe area.

![The six skills, one frame each](docs/skills.jpg)

| Skill | What it makes | Try it with |
|---|---|---|
| `/zach-d-films` | **A 3D cartoon "what if" explainer.** Cartoon people, props and effects built in three.js, slow-motion impacts, a red force ripple and captions timed to your voiceover. Comes with a finished 29 s example to build from. | `Could ancient armour stop an arrow?` |
| `/stick-figure` | **A stick-figure explainer reel.** A bright cartoon world, stick people with big faces, whip transitions, 1 to 2 word captions, and music and sound effects made in code. Comes with a finished 37 s example. | `Why did pirates wear eye patches?` |
| `/minimalistic-graphics` | **Black-and-white line art.** Hairline steps rise, one white dot hops up them and gets an orbit at the top, with one quiet line of text. | `Every step feels small until you look back` |
| `/map-route` | **A 3D map route.** A white city, a route that draws itself while the camera follows, a pin drop, an ETA that counts down and a destination card. | `Home to the gym, 2.8 km` |
| `/breakdown` | **A 3D exploded view.** A phone comes apart layer by layer, and every part gets a leader line and a label. | `My phone, every part labelled` |
| `/graph` | **A minimal line graph.** A smooth line draws itself, and one big number counts up with its tip. Black on white, or white on black. | `0 to 100K followers in 9 months` |

See them moving: **[novitckii.com/resources/animation-skills](https://novitckii.com/resources/animation-skills/)**

## Install

You need macOS or Linux with **ffmpeg**, **Node.js 18+** and **Python 3.9+**.

```bash
brew install ffmpeg node        # if you don't have them
git clone https://github.com/artemnovitckii/claude-animation-skills.git ~/claude-animation-skills
cd ~/claude-animation-skills && ./install.sh
```

`install.sh` links every skill into `~/.claude/skills/` (so they show up as `/graph`, `/map-route` and so on) and runs the one-time setup. The setup installs three.js and Playwright into `kit/node_modules`, fetches GSAP and warms up HyperFrames.

`/stick-figure` and `/zach-d-films` also need a free voice and word timings. They run on your computer, with no API key, and need about 1 GB of models, downloaded once:

```bash
./install.sh --voice
```

To update later, run `git pull && ./install.sh`.

**It's also packaged as a Claude Code plugin.** Run these inside Claude Code:
```
/plugin marketplace add artemnovitckii/claude-animation-skills
/plugin install animation-skills@claude-animation-skills
```
Plugin skills are namespaced (`/animation-skills:graph`). The git clone above is the route tested end to end.

```
/graph 0 to 100K followers in 9 months: …

# MyGo Music

A native desktop music player written in Go with [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo), no WebView. It plays your local files out of the box, and everything else comes from plugins.

## Features

- Local files (MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, WAV, and ALAC or AAC in .m4a and .aac) with tags, covers and `.lrc` lyrics
- Playlists, liked songs, search, albums and artists
- Now Playing with lyric stage styles, cover wall, queue, shuffle and repeat
- Notch player on macOS, tray, media keys
- Audio cache, fades on pause and seek, loudness normalization
- Session restore
- Podcast captions, written down on the device as episodes play
- English and Simplified Chinese
- Plugins can add accounts, catalogs, podcasts, stations, comments and pages of their own

## Build

```bash
go tool mygo dev     # run in development
go tool mygo build   # package into build/
go test ./internal/...
```

## Podcast captions

Episodes are written down on the device as they play, with [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) and Qwen3-ASR, which the app downloads when the listener asks for them. The libraries come from this repository's `sherpa-onnx-<version>` prerelease, which only changes with that version:

```bash
go run ./scripts/sherpa -sign "Developer ID Application: …"
gh release create sherpa-onnx-2.0.1 --prerelease --latest=false build/sherpa/*
```

## Plugins

A plugin is a folder in the app's `plugins` directory (Settings > Plugins > + > Show Plugins Folder) with a `plugin.json` and one JavaScript or TypeScript file. Install one with the + in Settings > Plugins from GitHub, by its repository or its address, or from its folder or a zip of it on this computer, or drop the folder in by hand. Remove one from its ⋯ menu there. There's nothing to build, and the same plugin runs on every platform. [`examples/demo-plugin`](examples/demo-plugin) does everything a plugin can with made-up data: copy it to start.

```json
{
  "id": "example",
  "name": "Example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "minAppVersion": "0.1.8",
  "main": "index.js",
  "playback": "stream",
  "permissions": { "network": ["api.example.com"] },
  "settings": [{ "key": "apiKey", "label": "API Key", "help": "From your account page", "link": "https://example.com/keys" }],
  "navigation": [
    { "builtin": "home" },
    { "title": "Charts", "page": "charts", "icon": "chart" },
    { "title": "Stations", "builtin": "stations" }
  ]
}
```

```js
export async function search({ query, kind, offset }) {
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&type=${kind}&offset=${offset}`, {
    headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${host.setting("apiKey")}` },
  });
  return { tracks: (await res.json()).items.map(toTrack), more: false };
}

export function stream({ id, quality }) {
  return { url: `https://api.example.com/audio/${id}.mp3`, type: "mp3" };
}
```

**Find out who causes your lag: your Wi-Fi, your router, your ISP or the game server.** [![Windows 10/11](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%20%7C%2011-0039A6?style=flat-square&logo=windows&logoColor=white)](#quick-start) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-1A1A1A?style=flat-square&logo=rust&logoColor=white)](#build-from-source) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-5F5F5F?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Portable](https://img.shields.io/badge/portable-no%20installer-0F7B0F?style=flat-square)](#quick-start) [![No admin](https://img.shields.io/badge/admin-not%20required-0F7B0F?style=flat-square)](#faq) [![No telemetry](https://img.shields.io/badge/telemetry-none-5F5F5F?style=flat-square)](#faq) [![Single exe](https://img.shields.io/badge/single-.exe-5F5F5F?style=flat-square)](#quick-start)
**Lag Doctor is a free ping test, packet loss test and jitter test for games on Windows.** It finds the server your game is actually connected to (CS2, VALORANT, Dota 2, Fortnite, Apex Legends, League of Legends and more), watches that connection live, and traces it hop by hop to tell you *where* the lag starts. No more guessing whether to restart the router, call your ISP or blame the servers: Lag Doctor shows the route as a line from your PC to the game server, colours every segment by health, and gives you a plain verdict with a fix.

## Why Lag Doctor ### Follows your real game server, automatically Start your game and Lag Doctor picks it up from the process list, reads the game's own connections and starts pinging the server it is really talking to. No IP to look up, no generic "speed test" to a server in another country. A fallback target (for example `1.1.1.1`) is used when no game is running. ### A blame meter that says who is at fault Every hop on the path is probed in rotation. Loss and jitter only count against a router when they **persist all the way to the server**, so routers that just rate-limit ICMP do not get blamed (the classic MTR reading rule). The result is a verdict you can act on: *your Wi-Fi*, *your router*, *your ISP* or *the game server*, with a confidence and the delay each segment adds.

These > builds evict unused pipelines after ~2.5 min, which freezes the game for ~20 s when a big pack is preloaded. > > **Optional warm-up** (once, and again after GPU driver updates): set the GPU's shader cache size to > 10 GB or Unlimited in your Nvidia control panel, turn preload on, boot the game, wait at the title screen until compiling finishes, > quit, then turn preload off. Every download is checksum-verified and validated; your previous cache is kept as `.bak`. ## Publishing a pack ``` lichii-sync pack -title [-prev .json] out/ - gh release create - out/ gh release upload manifests out/.json --clobber gh api -X PATCH repos///releases/$(gh api repos///releases/tags/- --jq .id) -f make_latest=false ``` Pack releases must not be marked *Latest*, or the README download button (the latest release page) shows a pack instead of the app. Upload the chunks before the manifest. 使用教程  在线体验

# Ocarina Recomp

[Read in English](README.en.md)

**Ocarina rodando nativo no Windows, sem emulador.**

O código do jogo é traduzido para C e compilado como um programa do Windows. Os gráficos do Switch 2 são convertidos para Vulkan. Tudo isso acontece **no seu PC, a partir do seu próprio arquivo do jogo**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Este repositório **não contém o jogo, keys nem executável**, e não explica como obtê-los. Você precisa da sua própria cópia. O que a instalação gera (o `ocarina.exe`, o código gerado, o cache de shaders e os saves) sai do seu jogo: **não compartilhe**.

## Estado do projeto

Experimental. Só foi testado em **um PC** (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, RTX 5090), na região do início do jogo.

| O quê | Situação |
|---|---|
| Abertura e jogo novo, até a Árvore Deku | ✅ Funciona |
| Vilarejo Kokiri: árvores, plantas, casas, luz | ✅ Funciona |
| Som, controle, saves e vídeos | ✅ Funciona |
| Desempenho na RTX 5090 | ✅ Cerca de 59 fps parado, 51 a 55 fps caminhando |
| Travadinhas ao entrar em áreas novas | ⚠️ Ainda acontecem, principalmente na primeira vez |
| Tocar a ocarina | ❓ Correção aplicada, ainda sem teste em jogo |
| Hyrule Field e o resto do jogo | ❓ Ainda não testados |
| Placas AMD e Intel | ❓ Nunca testadas |

## Como compilar

O jogo não vem pronto: ele é compilado no seu PC, a partir da sua cópia. Escolha um destes três jeitos.

**1. Com o instalador em ZIP, o mais fácil:** não instala nada no Windows e não pede administrador.

1. Baixe o **`Ocarina-Setup-...-windows.zip`** da [página de versões](https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp/releases/latest).
2. **Extraia o ZIP inteiro** para uma pasta e abra o `Instalar-Ocarina.exe` que está dentro dela.
3. O executável não tem assinatura digital, então o Windows pode avisar. Clique em **Mais informações** e depois em **Executar assim mesmo**.
4. Na janela, escolha o `.nup` do seu jogo (ou uma pasta com `exefs` e `romfs`) e clique em **Instalar**.
5. No fim, clique em **Jogar**, ou use o atalho **Ocarina Recomp** na Área de Trabalho.

Para desinstalar, apague a pasta de instalação. Prefere conferir antes? O executável só abre o script `instalador\Instalar-Ocarina.ps1`, que está ao lado dele no ZIP e pode ser lido em qualquer editor. O [código do executável](instalador/launcher.c) tem poucas linhas. Alguns antivírus reclamam de programas novos sem assinatura e de scripts do PowerShell: é um alarme possível, e o código está todo aqui para quem quiser conferir. A página de versões traz o SHA-256 do arquivo.

> [!NOTE]
> A etapa "Preparar os arquivos do jogo" é lenta, principalmente em HD: enquanto o relógio da janela andar, está funcionando.

**2. Com os scripts, que você pode ler antes de rodar** (instale antes as ferramentas do passo 1 do [guia](docs/compilar-manual.md)):

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp C:\OcarinaRecomp
cd C:\OcarinaRecomp
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\verificar.ps1 -Jogo "C:\caminho\seu-jogo.nup"
powershe…

# satmux

TCP multiplexer and `1-RTT` HTTP/TLS relay for geostationary (GEO) inflight Wi-Fi (Inmarsat GX, Viasat, Panasonic, SITA). Pure Python 3 stdlib, zero external dependencies.

Measured inflight over Inmarsat GX Ka-band (`~620 ms` RTT, SITA `AS206433` Amsterdam ground station):

```text
  ORIGIN (6× PARALLEL)  RAW CABIN WI-FI (:443)    1-RTT BBR + ZLIB MUX    SPEEDUP
  ────────────────────  ────────────────────────  ──────────────────────  ─────────
  GitHub Repo           ████████████    TIMEOUT  ███░░░░░░░░░    4.66s  FIXED ✓
  GitHub API            ████████████  TCP RESET  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.66s  FIXED ✓
  Hacker News           ████████████    TIMEOUT  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.28s  FIXED ✓
  MDN Docs              ████████░░░░     12.01s  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.30s     5.2×
  Cloudflare            ██░░░░░░░░░░      2.97s  █░░░░░░░░░░░    1.40s     2.1×
  PyPI JSON API         █████░░░░░░░      7.09s  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.64s     2.7×
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  6-Origin Burst:    19.13s (3/6 failed)  →  5.35s (0/6 failed)   [3.6× faster · -76% TTFB]
```

## Problem

Non-Starlink inflight Wi-Fi usually breaks on three things unrelated to raw bandwidth:

1. **Onboard `:443` middleboxes and DNS interception.** Cabin gateways intercept `:53` DNS and run a transparent `:443` split-TCP proxy (PEP) whose state table drops connections under load (`Connection reset by peer` / TLS timeouts on `github.com`, `api.github.com`, package registries). Non-443 TCP ports pass through untouched.
2. **Handshake round-trips (`~620 ms` per GEO hop).** Every new origin normally pays multiple satellite round-trips (DNS + TCP + TLS) before transferring payload bytes.
3. **Cubic congestion collapse.** Cabin Wi-Fi packet loss causes standard TCP to halve `cwnd` repeatedly, leaving most of your per-seat token-bucket cap unused.

## How it works

```text
Direct (:443):
  laptop ──▶ cabin DNS + :443 PEP ══(3–4 GEO RTTs)══▶ ground ──▶ origin  (frequent TCP resets)

satmux (:8444):
  laptop ══(12 persistent TCP :8444 BBR + zlib pipes)══▶ ground VM ──(2 ms)──▶ origin
```

- **Persistent non-443 carrier pool (`:8444`):** Keeps 12 pre-warmed TCP connections open to a Linux VM near the satellite ground station, bypassing the cabin `:443` proxy and onboard DNS. Streams are scheduled onto the carrier with the lowest recent byte load so idle browser keepalives do not cause head-of-line queueing.
- **0-RTT stream open (`127.0.0.1:1080` SOCKS5 / `127.0.0.1:8080` HTTP CONNECT):** Returns `OK` locally in `<1 ms` and sends `FT_OPEN` + TLS `ClientHello` in the same TCP burst, saving one full satellite RTT while preserving end-to-end TLS from the laptop.
- **1-RTT ground fetch (`127.0.0.1:8081`):** Sends an encrypted (`BLAKE2b-512` stream + `HMAC-SHA256`) request frame over a warm carrier. The ground VM performs DNS, verified TLS 1.3, and HTTP redirects on fiber (`~2–5 ms`) and compresses plaintext responses with `zlib` before crossing the sa…

# 🎯 Jenny Mod (Fapcraft) — Community Archive

**The ultimate interactive companion experience for Minecraft Java & Bedrock.**
Upgraded AI, restored models, and full compatibility with Forge 1.21 & MCPE.

[![Download Jenny Mod](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOWNLOAD_JENNY_ARCHIVE-ff69b4?style=for-the-badge&logo=windows&logoColor=white)](../../releases/latest)

![Jenny Mod Banner](https://i.postimg.cc/j5J3jw8n/a-high-quality-3d-render-in-th-2026-11-09T07-20-45-(1).png)

---

### 🧐 What is this Archive?

The **Jenny Mod** (also known as **Fapcraft**) is one of the most famous and sought-after mods in Minecraft history. It introduces fully interactive NPCs, a complex gift system, and a virtual girlfriend experience that goes far beyond standard villagers.

However, the original mod was abandoned on version 1.12.2. This repository serves as a **Community Archive**—a stable port that brings the full Jenny experience to modern versions of Minecraft (Forge 1.18 - 1.21.11) and Bedrock Edition (MCPE).

---

### 👥 Meet the Characters

Our archive includes all the classic characters, fully voiced and animated with upgraded AI pathfinding.

| Character | Role | Supported Platforms |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Jenny** | The iconic virtual girlfriend | Java, Bedrock |
| **Ellie** | The supportive companion | Java, Bedrock |
| **Bia** | The playful plush bear | Java |
| **Slime Girl** | The friendly slime hybrid | Java, Bedrock |
| **Goblin Girl** | The mischievous trader | Java |
| **Luna** | The neko fishergirl | Java |

---

### 📦 Installation Guide

We provide separate files for **Java Edition (Forge)** and **Bedrock Edition (MCPE)**. 

#### 🟢 For Java Edition (Forge 1.18 - 1.21.11)
1. Go to the **[Releases page](../../releases/latest)**.
2. Click the **Download** button in the latest release description.
3. Extract the ZIP file and find the `.jar` file for your version.
4. Place the `.jar` file into your `%appdata%\.minecraft\mods` folder.

# mightyCode

Run **Claude Code** on a local MLX model
([DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic](https://huggingface.co/xtools-at/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic)).
No API key needed, fully local (Apple Silicon only).

```
claude  --/v1/messages-->  anthropic_proxy.py  --/v1/chat/completions-->  mlx_lm.server (4-bit model)
```

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `claude-local` | Launcher. Starts the backend as a persistent service and opens `claude` |
| `anthropic_proxy.py` | Anthropic Messages API → OpenAI-compatible API proxy (streaming and tool calls supported) + EoCC compaction + Guard hook |
| `guard.py` | Tool-call inspection (exfiltration, credential access, persistence, destructive commands) |
| `convert_model.py` | HF → MLX 4-bit conversion (quantizes on CPU) |
| `setup.sh` | Creates the venv, downloads and converts the model, registers the command on PATH |

## Requirements
- Apple Silicon Mac (macOS), 16 GB RAM or more recommended
- Free disk space: about **25 GB** during conversion (19 GB source + 4.7 GB output). About 5 GB once the source is deleted
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (`brew install uv`)

## Installation

### 1. Claude Code itself (not included in this repository)
Claude Code cannot be redistributed, so install it yourself by following the official instructions.

```bash
# Official installer (macOS / Linux)
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
# or via npm (Node.js 18+)
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

claude --version   # verify
```
See https://code.claude.com/docs for the latest instructions. You do not need to log in with an Anthropic account to use it with a local model.

### 2. This repository
A pre-converted model is available at https://huggingface.co/shi3z/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic-MLX-4bit
(skip the 19 GB download and conversion: `hf download shi3z/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic-MLX-4bit --local-dir models/heretic-9b-mlx-4bit`, then run `./setup.sh`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/shi3z/mightyCode.git
cd mightyCode
./setup.sh
```
If you are short on disk space, put the conversion source on an external drive: `SRC_DIR=/Volumes/big/src ./setup.sh`
(If `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`.)

## Usage
```bash
claude-local          # start (first run takes a few tens of seconds to load the model). Arguments are passed through to claude
claude-local -p "..." # non-interactive run
claude-local status   # backend status
claude-local logs     # tail the logs
claude-local stop     # stop the backend (it keeps running after claude exits, so stop it when you no longer need it)
```

Environment variables:
| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MODEL_DIR` | `models/heretic-9b-mlx-4bit` | MLX model to use |
| `MLX_PORT` / `PROXY_PORT` | 8080 / 8082 | Ports |
| `THINKING` | 0 | Set to 1 to enable Qwen's thinking mode (slower) |
| `COMPACT_THRESHOLD` | 48000 | Estimated token count that trigg…

# lunar-for-roblox-decompiled

Decompiled output for Lunar for Roblox 1.0.16 (the Roblox launcher by
Moonsworth, not the Minecraft Lunar Client) - the Electron app, the NSIS
installer around it, and the native DLLs it ships with.

## Layout

- `src/` - main / preload / renderer bundles, cleaned up
- `installer/` - the NSIS script dumped to text, plus the uninstaller's
- `native/` - decompiled output (`.c`): `owutility*`/`integrity.c` up top,
  `installer/`, `addons/` and `chromium/` for the rest
- `docs/` - index of IPC channels/services, bundle outlines, owutility notes
- `tools/` - the scripts used to pull it apart

## Reproducing

```sh
# installer blocks + script dump
python tools/extract_nsis.py lunar-for-roblox-1.0.16-setup.exe out/
python tools/nsis_dump.py lunar-for-roblox-1.0.16-setup.exe script.txt

# the actual app payload is downloaded by the installer, grab it directly
curl -O https://appupdates.lunarrobloxprod.com/lunar-for-roblox-1.0.16-x64.nsis.7z
tar -xf lunar-for-roblox-1.0.16-x64.nsis.7z
npx @electron/asar extract resources/app.asar app
```

# Ram-Altman

**A bash script that writes to Sam Altman once a day to report the RAM he missed.**

Read the sample emails at **[ram-altman.lol](https://ram-altman.lol)**, no install needed.

[![Website: ram-altman.lol](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-ram--altman.lol-0f5a43)](https://ram-altman.lol)
![Global DRAM allocation: quite terrible](https://img.shields.io/badge/global%20DRAM%20allocation-quite%20terrible-red)
![Utilization: maybe 5%](https://img.shields.io/badge/utilization-maybe%205%25-orange)
![Emails: 1 per day](https://img.shields.io/badge/emails-1%20per%20day-blue)
![Written in Bash, not Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/written%20in-bash%2C%20not%20electron-brightgreen)

There is RAM in your computer. Right now. Just sitting there, in a *personal* computer, being personal.

You may have thought of this as "a computer working normally". On a recent episode of [Cheeky Pint](https://gizmodo.com/sam-altman-youre-completely-right-about-ram-im-sorry-for-the-confusion-heres-what-happened-2000835208), the CEO of OpenAI offered another view:

> "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer"
>
> — Sam Altman

That RAM, he added, is ["being used maybe 5% of the time"](https://www.xda-developers.com/sam-altman-says-its-quite-terrible-that-people-have-ram-in-their-pcs-during-a-shortage/).

Which raised an obvious question for a certain kind of person: *surely someone should be monitoring this?*

So we wrote a script. If your machine has more than 10% of its RAM available, it sends one email a day to let Sam know. It seemed only fair. He can't fix the problem if nobody tells him where the RAM is.

## Features

- Tracks total, used and available RAM, plus your standing with the global allocation authorities
- Handles page cache correctly, which already puts it ahead of most arguments about RAM
- Sends at most one email per day, because we're hoarders, not animals
- Rotates 8 subject lines, 10 messages and 6 sign-offs, so the joke gets old at a carefully managed pace
- Logs every sample to CSV for when the auditors arrive
- Ships with 14 tests, more than the DRAM market has had sensible outcomes
- Is written in bash, as an Electron version would have solved the problem by using all the RAM

## A sample of today's correspondence

```text
Subject: You missed a spot

Hi Sam,

Please don't be alarmed, but there is 8.6 GiB of RAM on my desk that isn't in
a data centre. That's 56.2% of what's installed here, and as far as I can tell
it has no plans today.

Hoarding responsibly,
A concerned RAM owner

--
Sent automatically, at most once a day, by a small script on one PC.
Reply if you'd like it to stop.
```

The figures are real. They come from your machine. That's the worrying part.

## What counts as "used"?

```text
used = MemTotal - MemAvailable
```

`MemAvailable` is the kernel's own estimate of how much memory programs c…

# CHIMERA

A physical-modeling voice synthesizer in the browser. Every sound comes from a simulated
airway (lungs, vocal folds or syrinx, a branched vocal tract, lips, nose), not from samples.
The engine is Rust, compiled to WebAssembly for an AudioWorklet; the same code runs natively
for tests and the `chimera` CLI.

## What it does

- **Play**: drag the tongue, lips and jaw in a live cutaway of the head; vowel pad, encoders,
  computer keyboard and Web MIDI.
- **Speak**: English text (CMUdict with a letter-to-sound fallback) or IPA, turned into
  gestures and prosody, with the gestural score and a consonant chart on screen.
- **Sing**: piano roll with lyrics per note; consonants land before the beat.
- **Beatbox**: pads and a step sequencer, every drum an articulatory gesture.
- **Bestiary**: songbird (two-voice syrinx), seal, alligator and elephant.
- **Duet** (`?show=<id>`): two 3D heads replay a pre-rendered song.

Male, female and child bodies blend continuously. Everything on screen animates from live
engine state: pressure in the airway, airflow, the vocal folds, spectra and formants.

## Run it

Needs Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, and Bun.

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # builds the wasm, then Vite on 127.0.0.1:5317
bun run test       # wasm build, cargo test --workspace, bun test tests
```

The AudioWorklet needs a secure context, so open it on localhost or over HTTPS (for example
`tailscale serve`). Vercel builds it with `vercel.json`.

Offline renders and measurement:

```sh
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- render speech|text|song|notes|beatbox|creature|vowels …
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- diagnose       # nasal leakage, formants, bandwidths, pitch
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- compare csd    # against a real singer (docs/csd-comparison.md)
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- compare tsp    # against 23 real speakers (docs/speech-comparison.md)
bun tools/spectrogram.ts in.wav out.png
```

## Docs

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the acoustic model (FDTD airway, sources,
  anatomy, gestures).
- [docs/rust-engine.md](docs/rust-engine.md): the engine's real-time and determinism contract,
  and the browser boundary.
- [docs/ui-redesign.md](docs/ui-redesign.md) and [docs/mockups/](docs/mockups/): the vector
  display look.
- [docs/csd-comparison.md](docs/csd-comparison.md): scoring the voice against the Children's
  Song Dataset.
- [docs/speech-comparison.md](docs/speech-comparison.md): scoring the speech against real
  speakers, phone by phone (the TSP speech database).
- [docs/hill-climb/](docs/hill-climb/): the rules and log for tuning the voice one measured
  step at a time.

Agents: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Bundled third-party files keep their own licenses: the CMU Pronouncing
Dictionary ([public/data/CMUDICT-LICENSE.txt](public/data/CMUDICT-LICENSE.txt)) and the fonts
([public/fonts/](public/fonts/)).

adriancmurray/symcache-prune.content:
# symcache-prune

TLDR: on some Macs, `/System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd` grows by gigabytes per hour and macOS
shows it only as "System Data". `symcache-prune` is one zsh script that installs an hourly launchd job which empties
that folder once it reaches 10 GB (or a size you choose). Check yours first:

```sh
sudo du -sh /System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd
```

## The problem

`coresymbolicationd` is the macOS daemon that turns addresses in binaries into symbol names, for crash reports,
debuggers, profilers and test tools. It keeps a cache, mostly one file named `data`, in
`/System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd`. Storage settings do not name it; it is counted as part of
"System Data". On one example machine, a development Mac running many test runs, the cache went from 0 to 9.4 GB in
about 5 hours and later reached 39 GB. Those are one machine's numbers; yours may grow much more slowly or not at all.

## Check yours

```sh
sudo du -sh /System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd
ls /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/coresymbolicationd_*.diag
```

The folder is readable only by root, so `du` needs `sudo`. It only reads sizes. The same command is printed by
`./symcache-prune check`.

The `.diag` files are resource reports. macOS writes one when a process writes more to disk than its allowed budget
over a period of time. A `coresymbolicationd` report names the event as disk writes, gives how much the daemon wrote
and over how long, the limit it went over, and stack samples of the code doing the writing. If you have several of
these, the cache is probably growing on your machine.

## Clear it by hand

```sh
sudo find -x /System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec rm -rf -- {} +
```

This deletes what is inside the folder and keeps the folder itself. The daemon rebuilds the cache as it needs it.

## Install, uninstall, status

Read the script before you run it as root; it is under 200 lines.

```sh
sudo ./symcache-prune install        # threshold 10 GB
sudo ./symcache-prune install 20     # threshold 20 GB; run again to change it
./symcache-prune status              # is the job loaded, last 5 log lines
sudo ./symcache-prune status         # the same, plus the cache size
sudo ./symcache-prune uninstall      # unload the job, remove the plist, the copy and the log
```

`install` writes:

- `/usr/local/libexec/symcache-prune`, a copy of the script (root:wheel, mode 755);
- `/Library/LaunchDaemons/local.symcache-prune.plist` (root:wheel, mode 644), label `local.symcache-prune`;
- `/var/log/symcache-prune.log`, created at the first prune.

`run [threshold-gb]` is what launchd calls. You can also call it yourself with `sudo`.

Run `zsh test` to check the script. It uses a temporary folder, needs no root and changes nothing on the system.

lxe/phoneuse.content: # Phone Use > [!WARNING] > **Under heavy construction.** This is a technology demo, and I have tested it on > one setup: an iPhone 17 Pro, Arch Linux, Hyprland and an NVIDIA GPU. Other setups > will likely need fixes. Phone Use lets your computer see and operate an unmodified iPhone. The iPhone sends its screen to the computer over AirPlay, and the computer sends taps and keystrokes to the iPhone as a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard, either through its own Bluetooth adapter or through the bridge: a small puck that sits near the phone and joins your Wi-Fi. You can use the phone from your computer yourself, or let an agent operate it from the command line or over MCP. The Phone Use app on the iPhone is where you allow and stop agents. It runs on Linux and macOS, and on Windows from source ([On Windows](#on-windows)). You don't need a jailbreak, a developer account or a cable. Phone Use relies on two features every iPhone has: Screen Mirroring and AssistiveTouch. ## Download **[Latest release](https://github.com/lxe/phoneuse/releases/latest)** | File | What it is | |---|---| | `PhoneUse--x86_64.flatpak` | Phone Use for Linux | | `PhoneUse--mac.dmg` | Phone Use for macOS 15 or later, signed and notarized | | `phoneuse-bridge-.bin` | Firmware for the bridge (a [LilyGO T-Display](https://github.com/Xinyuan-LilyGO/TTGO-T-Display)) | The iPhone app isn't in the App Store yet. To install it, build it from [`ios/`](ios/README.md) with Xcode onto your phone. ### Linux ```sh flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo flatpak install --user ./PhoneUse-0.1.2-x86_64.flatpak flatpak run co.lxe.PhoneUse ``` The window walks you through the rest: set up the bridge or turn on this PC's Bluetooth, pair the iPhone app, and start Screen Mirroring to "Phone Use on ". If a firewall blocks the iPhone, the window offers to open the ports. ### macOS Open the DMG, drag Phone Use to Applications, and open it. It lives in the menu bar and uses the bridge for input. ### The bridge The bridge is a [LilyGO T-Display](https://github.com/Xinyuan-LilyGO/TTGO-T-Display): an ESP32 board with a 1.14-inch screen, two buttons and USB-C. # fastmint-fcfs

**English** · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md)

**FCFS mint on BNB Smart Chain through Binance Agentic Wallet, landed in a block ±2 seconds after the sale opens.**

A skill for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and any other agent that reads `SKILL.md`) that fires a single mint/claim/buy transaction at the exact moment a sale opens, using a Binance Agentic Wallet (`baw` CLI). No private key on the machine: signing happens in Binance's backend through Developer Mode, the agent only prepares calldata and picks the moment.

```
sale opens (T)    T+0.05s          T+0.6–0.8s        T+1.3–1.5s       T+2.1–2.2s
   │                 │                  │                  │                 │
   ▼                 ▼                  ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 start ───► preview sent ───► simulation OK ───► BROADCASTED ───► in a block
         (NTP clock trigger)    (requestId)     (baw execute)     (receipt)
```

The numbers above were measured 11 Nov 2026 from Indonesia: 3 time-gated dry-runs plus one real mint (Pocket Moons, 2 free NFTs, trigger→receipt 2.0 seconds). The previous sequential version took 5–6 seconds.

---

## Table of contents

1. [How it works](#1-how-it-works)
2. [Installation](#2-installation)
3. [Usage flow](#3-usage-flow)
4. [Command reference](#4-command-reference)
5. [Dynamic arguments](#5-dynamic-arguments)
6. [Safety rails](#6-safety-rails)
7. [Measured numbers](#7-measured-numbers)
8. [Troubleshooting](#8-troubleshooting)
9. [File layout](#9-file-layout)
10. [FAQ](#10-faq)

---

## 1. How it works

### Why the old version was slow

`baw` has no direct-send command for a contract call. The flow is two steps by design: `contract-call preview` (the backend simulates and returns a `requestId`) and then `contract-call execute --requestId`. The old version waited for a public RPC to report a successful `eth_call` (±1 second after the opening block), then previewed, then executed. Every stage waited on the previous one: T+5–6 seconds.

### Three parallel triggers

`fire.js` does not wait on a single signal. During the 3-second **burst** window after the sale opens, three triggers may each launch a preview independently (minimum spacing `--gap` 350ms, at most `--inflight` 3 at a time):

| trigger | when | source |
|---|---|---|
| **clock** | exactly T+0 by the NTP-corrected clock | `sntp` to time.apple.com / pool.ntp.org |
| **head** | the first block with `timestamp ≥ start` is seen | WebSocket `newHeads` (QuikNode, publicnode, drpc) + HTTP polling every 150ms |
| **eth_call OK** | a simulation from the wallet succeeds on one of the 4 fastest RPCs | `eth_call` on tags `latest` and `pending`, every 100ms |

The first preview that comes back with `simulationCode 000000000` is executed immediately, **exactly once**. Other previews still in flight are ignored. Previews that fail because the backend has not seen the opening block yet (error `351805`) are cheap and harmless; the next trigger retries…

# 星瑶 (Y-code)

[English](README.en.md) | 中文

> 一个国产终端 AI 编程助手，代号「星瑶」。支持 TUI 控制台与 GUI 窗口双形态、多模型切换、子代理编排、计划执行、长期记忆、MCP 扩展与可插拔技能系统。

> **使用须知**：本项目是运行在你本地设备上的 AI 编程辅助工具，自身不提供模型服务，模型需你自行配置并直接与其通信。AI 生成内容可能不准确、需你自行审查验证；软件具备文件读写与命令执行能力，请在使用前阅读下方「免责条款」——安装向导与首次启动都会提示确认。

## ✨ 功能亮点

### 对话与界面

- **终端交互界面**：基于 `prompt_toolkit` 的 Claude Code 风格输入框，支持斜杠命令、Tab 补全、`@文件` 快速挂载、多行粘贴
- **GUI 窗口版**：基于 `pywebview` + Vue 3 + TypeScript 的图形界面，与 CLI 共享同一套核心引擎
- **GUI 拖拽附件**：拖入文件即上屏占位并自动补全真实路径，PDF 等二进制文件注入路径提示供模型用工具解析
- **文件树面板**：懒加载子目录，支持手动刷新与页签激活/窗口聚焦自动刷新，展开状态可恢复；点击图片（png/jpg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/svg）可直接弹窗预览
- **GUI 面板宽度自定义**：侧栏 / 右面板分界线可拖拽调整宽度（双击恢复默认），宽度记忆到本地重启仍生效
- **9 种终端主题**：cyan / matrix / nord / cyberpunk / dracula / lava / sunset / amber / white，`/theme` 一键切换
- **终端 Markdown 渲染**：代码块语法高亮、表格、列表等富文本展示
- **思考流显示**：实时呈现模型推理过程（`<thinking>` 标签解析 + 句子边界缓冲）

### 模型与工具

- **多模型管理**：通过 `/models` 打开全屏模型选择器，支持 OpenAI / Anthropic / DeepSeek / Agnes 等多种协议，由自研 HTTPX 引擎（`core/llm_native_transport.py`）统一调用
- **副模型机制**：可配置副模型承担视觉识别、记忆压缩、子代理调用等任务，主副分工
- **29 个内置工具**：文件读写、代码搜索、命令执行、网页抓取、图片下载与生图、天气查询、LSP 符号查找、计划编排、智能路由等
- **工具结果缓存**：相同搜索/读取自动走本地缓存，节省 token 与时间

### 核心内核（Harness）

- **固定主代理内核**：严格状态机（Turn 8 态 / Step 10 态），非法状态转移显式失败；内核非插件化、不可动态替换
- **SQLite Journal**：owner 租约 + 心跳防多进程冲突，事件序列单调分配，消息与事件同事务原子提交
- **崩溃恢复**：未完成回合仅标记为 `interrupted`，绝不自动重放模型请求、命令或文件写入等副作用
- **请求指纹**：对最终 Provider 请求生成不可变指纹，配合 byte-golden 回归防止缓存漂移
- **工具管线**：同签名重复调用抑制（RepeatCallGuard），相邻只读工具并发批量执行

### 高级编排

- **子代理系统**：5 种内置类型（explore / implement / test / review / general）+ 自定义子代理，支持依赖感知并行调度与嵌套（最深 3 层）
- **计划执行模式**：多步任务（拆解后子任务超过 3 条）先用 `plan_write` 建立可执行计划，按依赖图逐项派发子代理，支持暂停 / 恢复 / 重试 / 取消
- **后台任务管理**：长周期命令后台执行，`/tasks` 查看状态、`/tasks tail` 看日志、`/tasks kill` 终结
- **权限系统**：四种模式（confirm 变更前确认 / accept_edits 自动编辑 / plan 计划模式 / full 完全访问），沙盒控制工作目录访问边界

### 记忆与上下文

- **SQLite 会话记忆**：多会话切换；撤销不改写历史，聊天完整保留
- **按回合撤销**：每个回合的受控文件修改持久化快照，`/undo` 整轮预检后一键撤销；冲突零写入、崩溃可恢复，模型通过上下文得知文件结果已失效
- **长期记忆系统**：四类记忆（user / feedback / project / reference）+ 每日日志 + Dream 整理线程，支持「记住 XXX」指令
- **智能记忆压缩**：历史 token 占用达 70% 自动压缩，工具结果预截断，tiktoken 精确估算
- **会话导出**：`/share` 一键导出为 Markdown / HTML / JSON

### 扩展生态

- **技能系统（Skills）**：扫描 `SKILL.md` 并动态注入系统提示词，支持项目级与用户级
- **插件系统（Plugins）**：进程内插件扩展工具能力，零核心侵入，单插件异常不影响启动；内置混元文生图插件，支持用户级插件热加载

# IZCIVSwitch

IZCIVSwitch is a PC-side research toolkit for Nintendo Switch 2 and Civilization VII.

**PC compatibility.** The bundled Lobby runtime targets Linux x86_64.

[Release notes](https://github.com/byizmysh/IZCIVSwitch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) · [Safety notice](DISCLAIMER.md)

> **Use with caution.** This research software can modify game save data and cause the console to freeze. Back up your saves before use. A freeze may require a full power cycle. Use the software only with hardware and content you are authorized to access. It comes without a warranty.

## Installation

**Checksums.** The repository's `SHA256SUMS` records the files at tag `v0.1.0`. For release archives, use the separate SHA-256 checksum file under **Assets** on the release page.

> **Read this section first.** The release archive does **not** contain `prod.keys`. You must supply your own console dump for the PC-side Lobby injection.

### 1. Download and extract

| Package | Use |
|---|---|
| `IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Full package: kit + PC Lobby runtime + launcher; Linux x86_64 |
| `IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0-source.zip` | Scripts + kit + launcher, no Lobby runtime; use with an existing `iz2s-panel` or the Switch 1 NRO |

Extract the **entire** archive to a writable folder. Do not run from inside the archive.

```text
IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0/
├── IZCIVSwitch.py
├── pc-install-trigger.py
├── kit/                         # original civswitch-kit
├── panel/                       # PC-side CivSwitchLDN (full archive only)
│   └── data/
│       ├── runtime/civswitchldn/
│       └── private/civswitchldn/   <-- prod.keys goes here
├── izlauncher/                  # optional menu
├── README.md
├── DISCLAIMER.md
└── RELEASE_NOTES.md
```

### 2. Provide `prod.keys`

`prod.keys` is **required only for the PC-side Lobby injection** (`IZCIVSwitch.py --lobby` and `pc-install-trigger.py`). It is **not needed** for `IZCIVSwitch.py --no-lobby` / XSTRIG, and it is **not included** in the release.

Place your own `prod.keys` here:

```bash
panel/data/private/civswitchldn/prod.keys
```

Recommended permissions:

```bash
chmod 700 panel/data/private/civswitchldn
chmod 600 panel/data/private/civswitchldn/prod.keys
```

The file is a standard text `prod.keys` dump from **your own console**. It must contain at least these 32-hex-character entries (the LDN panel checks them):

```
aes_kek_generation_source
aes_key_generation_source
master_key_00
master_key_12
```

`title.keys` is not required for the Lobby injector. Do not download keys from untrusted sources, and never commit them to a repository.

If you do not have `prod.keys`, skip the Lobby path and use the Switch 1 NRO from the original kit to install `XSTRIG.Civ7Save`; after that, `IZCIVSwitch.py --no-lobby` needs no keys.

### 3. Restore raw-socket capabilities

The bundled Lobby runtime needs `cap_net_admin` and `cap_net_raw` on:

```text
panel/data/runtime/civswitchldn/bin/python-ldn

HybridRobotics/supermimic.content:
# SuperMimic

[Project page](https://supermimic.github.io) | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)

SuperMimic trains a humanoid whole-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model, built on [mjlab](https://github.com/mujocolab/mjlab).

## Setup

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Clone both repos as siblings:

```bash
mkdir supermimic_ws && cd supermimic_ws
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/supermimic.git
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/mjlab_research.git
cd supermimic
```

## Usage

Available task IDs:

- `SuperMimic-GenCoord-G1` — generalized coordinates representation
- `SuperMimic-MaxCoord-G1` — maximal coordinates representation

Train a world model and policy:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<GPU_ID> uv run src/supermimic/scripts/train.py \
  <TASK_ID> --runner.run_name <description>
```

Play back a trained model:

```bash
uv run src/supermimic/scripts/play.py \
  <TASK_ID> --wandb-path <RUN_PATH>
```

## Acknowledgements

SuperMimic contains code inspired by these projects:

- [ControlVAE](https://github.com/heyuanYao-pku/Control-VAE) (BSD-3-Clause)
- [robotic_world_model](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/robotic_world_model) (Apache-2.0)
- [DreamerV3](https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3) (MIT)

## License

Copyright 2026 The SuperMimic Authors.

Released under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

# Goodle Drive — Cloud Storage UI

Template dashboard penyimpanan cloud yang dibuat dengan HTML, CSS, dan JavaScript. Desain biru dengan sidebar melengkung, kartu folder, dan daftar file interaktif.

[**Buka demo**](https://laluarifta.github.io/goodle_drive_cloud_storage_ui/)

## Preview

![Preview dashboard Goodle Drive](assets/img/preview.png)

## Menjalankan

Clone repository lalu buka `index.html` di browser:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LALUARIFTA/goodle_drive_cloud_storage_ui.git
cd goodle_drive_cloud_storage_ui
```

Atau jalankan server lokal jika Python tersedia:

```bash
python -m http.server 8000
```

Buka <http://localhost:8000>. Tidak diperlukan backend untuk mencoba template.

## Struktur

```text
.
├── index.html          # Halaman utama
├── assets/
│   ├── css/            # Stylesheet frontend
│   ├── js/             # Logika interaksi dashboard
│   └── img/
│       └── preview.png # Preview untuk README
├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## Fitur antarmuka

- Layout responsif dengan menu sidebar untuk layar kecil.
- Pencarian file, filter folder, serta tampilan daftar dan grid.
- Navigasi My Drive, Computers, Shared With Me, Recents, Trash, Starred, dan Backups.
- Preview file, penandaan bintang, serta pengelolaan sampah dalam sesi demo.

## Kustomisasi

- Ubah struktur halaman dan identitas produk di `index.html`.
- Ubah warna dan tampilan di `assets/css/`.
- Ubah data contoh dan perilaku dashboard di `assets/js/app.js`.
- Ganti `assets/img/preview.png` untuk memperbarui screenshot README.

## Publikasi

Repository ini disajikan melalui **GitHub Pages**, dari branch `main` dan folder `/` (root). Semua path aset relatif sehingga dapat digunakan pada project site GitHub Pages maupun hosting statis lain.

Untuk repository hasil fork, aktifkan **Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → main → / (root)**, lalu perbarui URL demo pada README.

Ini **template frontend/demo**, bukan layanan Google Drive dan tidak berafiliasi dengan Google. # BlinkMimic 2

**One humanoid motion-tracking policy for all 129,491 clips of BONES-SEED, trained in about 15 minutes on one RTX 4090.**

[SuperMimic](https://supermimic.github.io/) ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480),
[code](https://github.com/HybridRobotics/supermimic)) showed that one policy can track a whole motion library when it
is trained by backpropagating through a learned, differentiable world model of the robot. On BONES-SEED it reached the
tracking quality of [SONIC](https://doi.org/10.1126/scirobotics.aed4592) (trained on 128 GPUs for about a week) with
one H100 in about three hours. [InstantTrack](https://github.com/Huy-Quang-Dao/instantTrack) and
[BlinkMimic](https://github.com/fuyichen0725/blinkmimic) made this learner much faster on the 40 clips of LAFAN1.

BlinkMimic 2 brings this speed to the full BONES-SEED library and studies which changes make training faster.
**One policy for all 129,491 clips trains in 15.5 minutes on one RTX 4090, with 17 failed clips** (mean of three
seeds). The main changes are exams, in which simulated robots play whole clips as the evaluation does, and a step size
planned for the short run ([how it works](#how-it-works)).

![Training time of reported BONES-SEED results, log scale](docs/media/time_comparison.png)

*Training time to each reported result on BONES-SEED (log scale). The other bars are the numbers each project
reports, with its own evaluation and hardware, so they are not on one scale; realmimic's released weights are also
scored by our evaluation. Sources: [SuperMimic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480),
[supermimic-prime](https://github.com/xkhainguyen/supermimic-prime),
[SuperMimic-Reproduced](https://github.com/CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced),
[realmimic](https://github.com/kevinhenryzz/realmimic),
[SuperMimic-Rep](https://github.com/LaoYang1994/SuperMimic-Rep),
[supermimic_vibe](https://github.com/dhmbb2/supermimic_vibe),
[SONIC](https://doi.org/10.1126/scirobotics.aed4592) (as scored by SuperMimic).*

![Backflip, hip-hop dance, high jump, fall and get up](docs/media/hero.gif)
![Spinning turns, crawl, sitting cross-legged, push-ups](docs/media/more.gif)

*One trained policy in the simulator, each clip played from its first frame. Solid: robot; translucent blue: the
reference motion. Every clip shown was tracked to its end in the evaluation on all clips and in at least 137 repeated
runs.*

## Results

| | training | clips tracked to the end | failed clips | tracking score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **BlinkMimic 2** (mean of 3 seeds) | **15.5 min**, one RTX 4090 | **99.987%** | **17** of 129,491 | **0.946** |
| [realmimic](https://github.com/kevinhenryzz/realmimic) released weights, for scale | about 10.5 h, one RTX 4090 | 99.988% | 16 of 129,491 | 0.950 |

Every clip is played once from its first frame in the simulator, without randomization, and both rows are scored by
the same evaluation.

- **Failed clip**: the robot falls or drifts away from the reference before the clip ends …

# Toyxyz Blender Retargeter

Transfer natural-looking humanoid motion between rigs with different body proportions in Blender 5.0 or later. Proportion-aware root travel, adjustable limb reach, and foot contact help adapt stride and foot placement to the target rig while preserving the source motion. Preview the result live and bake it to a Blender Action.

[Download the latest release](https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz-blender-retargeter/releases/latest) · [Read the user guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md)

## Demo

Both videos use the same source motion and the same three target rigs, with short, standard, and long legs.

### Toyxyz Blender Retargeter

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/784f2eaa-0a1a-4120-929a-e4eb2ae73ccd

### FK-only comparison

The target rigs use direct FK rotation copying without the add-on.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92e0edd6-31b7-4b0c-9bfd-5ca1aa047eb9

## Add-on interface

![Retarget sidebar with three connected actors and controls for baking, solver options, reference poses, and bone mapping](docs/images/addon-interface.png)

## Quick start

1. Download the add-on ZIP and install it from **Preferences → Get Extensions → Install from Disk**.
2. Open the **Retarget** tab in the 3D Viewport sidebar. Choose the **Source** and **Target** armatures.
3. Click **Bone Mapping → Build Bones List**, review the assignments, and click **Connect**.
4. Preview the motion and click **Bake to Action** when you are ready to edit the result.

## Features

- Live retargeting for multiple rig pairs, with per-actor settings
- Automatic bone matching, manual mapping, and reusable JSON presets
- Editable reference poses, limb reach, root travel, and foot contact
- Single-actor and batch baking to Blender Actions

Hand contact control is currently limited, including the ability to keep the palms planted during weight-bearing motions.

## Build from source

Run `blender --command extension build --source-dir .` from the repository root.

# Flash ALOHA: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation

Project website: johnyao93.github.io/flash-aloha

Data collection, training and deployment for bimanual and single-arm manipulation
with ARX arms (L5 and Trossen_L5): camera servers, hand-guided recording, ACT
and Flow policy training, direct and remote inference, and visualization.

Two policies are included: decoder-only ACT (the default) and Flow, which uses the
LeRobot U-Net/visual backbone. Both support training-time RTC prefix conditioning
and optional image/proprioceptive masking. The remote client can also execute an
OpenPI server's policy (for example Pi0.5); see `docs/image_preprocessing.md`.

## Quick start

The steps below are each described in their own section. Commands that move a robot
are marked operator-run: read the section before running them.

```bash
# 1. Install and run the offline tests (no robot needed)
uv sync --extra dev && source .venv/bin/activate && source scripts/setup/paths.sh
python -m pytest

# 2. Connect an arm, then tune its gravity and friction compensation
uv run scripts/tune.py gravity L5 can0              # MODEL INTERFACE
uv run scripts/tune.py friction L5 can0

# 3. Practice: move the arm by hand, then record a motion and replay it (no cameras, nothing saved)
uv run scripts/practice.py --arm right
uv run src/recording/replay_practice.py --arms right

# 4. Save a start pose and record demonstrations
uv run scripts/setup/set_up_recording.py --task_name single_arm
python scripts/run.py collect single_arm

# 5. Train, then run the policy
python scripts/run.py train single_arm_act
python scripts/run.py infer single_arm_act
```

`single_arm` (one ARX arm, two cameras) and `bimanual` (two ARX arms, three cameras)
are the example tasks in `src/config/tasks/`; copy one to describe your own setup.

## Setup

Run commands from the repository root. Once per terminal:

```bash
uv sync --extra dev
source .venv/bin/activate
source scripts/setup/paths.sh
python -m pytest                    # offline: synthetic observations, simulated hardware
```

The tests never start a camera or a robot controller. `.python-version` selects
Python 3.10.

Build the ARX SDK's Python extension on the robot computer following
[src/hardware/arx5-sdk/README.md](src/hardware/arx5-sdk/README.md) (its Conda environment
supplies the native dependencies). `paths.sh` expects that environment at
`$HOME/miniconda3/envs/arx-py310`; set `ARX_CONDA_PREFIX` if yours is elsewhere, and
`OROCOS_KDL_PYTHON` if you built PyKDL from source.

The files under `calibration/` were measured on one physical setup and are examples
only: recalibrate for your own arms and cameras before use
([calibration/README.md](calibration/README.md)).

Datasets, checkpoints and logs default to `data/`, `ckpts/` and `logs/` in the
repository root and are not part of the repository. To keep them elsewhere, for
example on a larger disk, set any of:

```bash
export FLASH_ALOHA_DATA_DIR=/path/to/datasets
export FLASH_ALOHA_CKPT_DI…

Shape

Shape decodes captured request headers into named signal fields. You can inspect those fields, change supported values, and encode the full decoded payload back into headers while retaining its other signals and report channels. For a new capture, trace its VM seed into readable JavaScript and use that program with the matching session to compile a decode artifact. Save the artifact to decode later requests from that build and session without repeating the source analysis. You can also deobfuscate the kernel and name recovered functions to investigate how signals are collected. Use the CLI for one-off work with files, or load an artifact once in the SDK for repeated calls from your application. # ScanDot

[![CI](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

ScanDot is an experimental Android app for capturing and viewing 3D point clouds on a supported phone. It combines ARCore camera tracking and depth estimates, saves scans locally, and provides an interactive viewer.

The repository also contains a separate video photogrammetry pipeline that runs on a workstation using FFmpeg and COLMAP. **The Android app does not reconstruct ordinary video with photogrammetry on the phone.**

## Current status

- Capture, save and reopen point clouds on devices that support ARCore Depth.
- Rotate, pan and zoom scans in the viewer. An optional full-depth mode interpolates missing depth and can distort surfaces.
- Prepare video frames and run a sparse or dense COLMAP reconstruction on a workstation.

This is an early prototype. Results can contain gaps, drift and noise; they are not textured meshes or validated measurements. Reflective, transparent and textureless subjects are difficult. Capture quality and device compatibility need further testing.

## Try the preview

Download the [preview APK](https://github.com/faizfahmi77/ScanDot/releases/tag/v0.3.0-preview.1). The release notes describe compatibility and signing limitations.

## Build the Android app

You need JDK 17, Android SDK 36, and an Android device with ARCore Depth support. Camera permission is required; Google Play Services for AR may require installation or an update.

```sh
cd android-app
./gradlew assembleDebug lintDebug testDebugUnitTest
```

On Windows, use `gradlew.bat` in place of `./gradlew`. The debug APK is written to `android-app/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. Install it as an update to preserve existing app data.

In the app, name the scan, tap **Start scan**, and move slowly around the subject in good light. Save it, then open it from **Results**. Scans are stored in the app's private storage; uninstalling the app removes them.

## Workstation video pipeline

The benchmark requires Python 3.12 or newer, FFmpeg, FFprobe and a compatible COLMAP installation. Dense reconstruction requires a compatible COLMAP configuration. From the repository root:

```sh
python -m processing.benchmark prepare "path/to/input.mp4" --output "path/to/new-run" --fps 5
python -m processing.benchmark reconstruct "path/to/new-run" --colmap "path/to/colmap" --dense
```

The output directory must not already exist. Omit `--dense` for a sparse-only run. See the subcommand `--help` output for options. A successful run does not establish complete or accurate geometry.

The Python tests use the standard library:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Project structure

```text
android-app/  Android capture, local storage and point-cloud viewer
processing/   Video preparation and COLMAP orchestration
tests/        Python tests with synthetic fixtures
tools/        Workstation utilities…

# 屏幕教学助手 · guide-tutor

在 Windows 桌面上"手把手"教用户操作：一个置顶悬浮球负责读屏，一层全屏透明标注层画箭头/圆圈/矩形，一块可调透明度的半透明面板写当前该做什么，外加一个本地 Markdown 知识库存教学步骤。

由两部分组成：

- **DSH Host 插件**（`index.js`）：注册 `guide_*` 工具、管理知识库、拉起并守护悬浮层进程、提供本机 HTTP / SSE 实时接口。
- **原生 WPF 悬浮层**（`native/overlay.ps1`）：悬浮球、标注层、面板三扇窗口，全程置顶、标注层鼠标穿透。

## 现在能做什么

| 能力 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 读屏 | 点球（或面板上的「读屏」）→ 悬浮层自动隐藏 0.2 秒截图 → 宿主把截图作为一条消息发给当前对话 → 模型读图后标注 |
| 屏幕标注 | `rect` / `circle` / `arrow` / `text` / `spotlight`，可带小标签，坐标与截图 1:1 |
| 半透明面板 | 标题、正文（建议 ≤30 字，可拖选复制，右上 `⧉` 一键复制整块）、步骤列表（当前步高亮）、35–100% 透明度滑块、可折叠成球；输入框支持 `Ctrl+V` 与右键粘贴 |
| 时钟 | 球下面常驻 `HH:mm`，面板标题栏常驻 `HH:mm:ss`；每 120ms 的 tick 只在秒数变化时重画，不额外占 CPU |
| 大小可调 | 面板底部「大小」滑块拖动即可，70%–180% 连续可调（松手 0.4 秒后落盘）；球上 `Ctrl+滚轮` 一档 5%。只缩放上半部分（标题/正文/步骤/下一步），底部操作条保持原大——否则滑块会跟着自己变长，一拖就冲到顶。值存进 `state.json` 的 `panel.uiScale`，重启后还在 |
| 知识库 | `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\guide-tutor\kb\*.md` 与 `*.docx`，模型可读写，下次直接复用步骤 |
| Word 文档 | `guide_kb` 存 `.docx` 时用 Markdown 生成排版好的 Word（标题/列表/表格）；也能导入、读取已有 `.docx` |
| 语音播报 | 回复用本机 SAPI 中文语音念出来，屏幕出现逐字渐显的字幕，字幕与语音按词同步；**回复会被拆成一句一句念**，句间停顿，像人在说话，而不是压成一句概括 |
| 触发时机 | 以 DSH 的持久 `turn/end` 事件为准：面板发消息、DSH 输入框打字、语音输入都会触发朗读，不再依赖某条输入路径 |
| 对话记录 | 面板标题栏的「记录」：列出插件端最近的对话流水（时间、谁说的、从哪说、内容），数据存在 `chatlog.json`，只留最近 120 条，纯本机 |
| 时间检测 | 每 60 秒一次心跳（`tickIntervalSec` 可改）：记下当前时间、写 `ticks.jsonl`、广播 SSE `tick` 事件，并挨个调用 `registerTickHandler` 订阅者。现在给计划/待办提供时间基准，也是以后子代理「到点读屏上报」的接入点 |
| 字幕定位 | 字幕出现在最近一次标注旁边（标注下方，放不下就放上方）；没有标注时在屏幕底部居中 |
| 语音 | 面板「说」按钮或 `Ctrl+Alt+V`：本地离线 sherpa-onnx paraformer 识别中文（不联网、不要 key）→ 作为一条【语音】消息发给模型 → 模型照常看屏/标注 |
| 面板对话 | 面板底部输入框写目标/问题，回车发送：模型先和你确认目标、列计划，你说「开始」它才开始标注 |
| 收尾 | 面板「✓」或 `guide_finish`：模型先截屏核验，再清空标注、面板折叠回球，任务标记完成 |
| 实时接口 | 本机 HTTP + SSE + 浏览器状态页，外部脚本也能驱动标注与读屏 |
| 托盘图标 | 任务栏托盘一个「引」图标：左键打开面板，右键菜单可读屏一次 / 切换常听 / 隐藏悬浮层 / 退出 |
| 下一步按钮 | 面板底部「下一步 ›」：表示这步做完了，宿主自动截屏并把下一步交给模型（也可 `POST /next`） |
| 常听 | 面板「常听」勾选框或托盘菜单：说完一句自动继续听；连续 5 次没听清会自动关闭并提示 |
| 语音音色 | 默认 **Edge 晓晓**（`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`，神经网络音色，需联网）；断网或合成失败自动回落到系统 SAPI「惠惠」。换音色：`index.js` 的 `config.edgeVoice`（可选 `zh-CN-YunxiNeural`、`zh-CN-YunyangNeural`、`zh-CN-XiaoyiNeural`、`zh-CN-liaoning-XiaobeiNeural` 等 14 个中文音色）；想完全离线用 `config.ttsEngine: 'sapi'` |
| 桌面清单 | 目标排成当天的**真实时间轴**，贴右缘、满屏高：每条一个块，**块高由内容决定**（标题自动换行，长课也一样完整显示），只有空档 ≥25 分钟才画一条 `06:00–08:30` 这样的细分隔线，一天排到 22:30；点 ☐ 打勾/取消、每条右侧 **✎ 改**（弹预填窗口）/ **✕ 删**、拖标题栏、点 ✕ 收起、点 ⚙ 开设置（清单透明度/宽度、悬浮球透明度、面板透明度/大小、提醒语气）、点标题栏 **＋** 自己加一条任务（填开始/结束/地点/做什么，`HH:mm`，手填的时间原样落盘，不往番茄钟上拗）；**空档行右侧还有一个淡淡的 ＋**，点了直接用那一段的开始时间预填（结束 +25 分钟），不用手改时间。数据在 `plan.json`，卡片读 `state.plan` + `state.card`，是无边框 + 强半透明的「伪融入」，不是真嵌壁纸层 |
| 顶部任务条 | 屏幕顶端一行，显示**当前时段**该做的事，带**秒级**倒计时（`15:26–15:51　秒级倒计时测试　@ 宿舍　·　剩 24:03`，每秒跳）；当前没有条目时退而显示 30 分钟内即将开始的一条（前缀「接着」，显示「12:30 后」），都没有就自动隐藏。拖动可移动；右端「−/＋」或直接滚轮调大小（0.7–2.0，0.1 一档）；位置与大小存 `state.json` 的 `topbar`，重启还在 |

## 安装

已经装在本机的 desktop profile 里（`link:` 到本目录）。重装 / 更新：

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=<本目录绝对路径>
```

**注意**：Host 半代码改动后必须重启 DSH 应用才会生效（没有运行时热重载）；悬浮层脚本 `native/overlay.ps1` 改动后只需 `guide_overlay restart`。
