[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/deslop-please.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/deslop-please)

An opinionated linter to remove sloppy code. It follows [*A Philosophy of Software Design*](https://www.amazon.com/Philosophy-Software-Design-John-Ousterhout/dp/1732102201): 
**deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces. 


```bash
cargo install deslop-please
```

```bash
> deslop-please

error[field-leak]: `RunQueue::items` is known outside `RunQueue`: 4 places in 2 modules
  --> src/sched/policy.rs:7:1
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:7:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::admit`
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:12:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::next`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:4:1: `runqueue::sched::report::backlog`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:8:1: `runqueue::sched::report::drained`
    runqueue::queue::ring::RunQueue
      items ◀━┳━ 2  runqueue::sched::policy
              ┗━ 2  runqueue::sched::report
      also known outside: head
      kept: limit

deslop-please: 65535 errors, well done!
```

### It's not my fault 

Sure, let's just mute them:

```bash
deslop-please --update-allow .deslop-please.allow  
deslop-please --allow .deslop-please.allow 
```

### Add to your `AGENTS.md`

```markdown
-  Run [`deslop-please`](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please) to check for sloppy code structure.
-  Errors flagged by `deslop-please` must be fixed from first principles, don't do mechanical moves to hide them.
    - `module-cycle` & `tangle`: what is the indented layer of abstraction? Which module should be at which layer?
    - `field-leak` & `shallow-module`: Why we have these fields/functions at all? What are the patterns of use? Can they be hidden behind a narrow interface? Don't fix each leak one at a time, fix them holistically.
    - Draw a diagram to help user understand the before and proposed after structure.
```

## Why they are sloppy 

They are really just one single idea: **deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces.

Deep modules hide the attention for you and your agents, so you only need to care about the narrow interface.

# Minecraft Server on Orange Cloud

Put your Minecraft server behind the orange cloud! No VPS to patch and no ports to forward.

This runs a [Paper](https://papermc.io) server for Minecraft Java entirely on Cloudflare. You deploy it with one command into your own Cloudflare account, and players join at a hostname on your domain.

![Players connect over TCP to Spectrum, then a Worker and a Durable Object, which starts the Paper container and answers while it wakes. The container saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes.](assets/how-it-works.png)

## How it works

1. [Spectrum takes the player's TCP connection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/how-to/route-tcp-traffic-to-a-worker/) on port 25565 and hands it to a Worker.

2. The Worker passes the connection to a Durable Object, which starts the [Paper container](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/) and relays bytes to it.

3. After 10 minutes with nobody online, the server saves the world and sleeps. The next player to connect wakes it in about 30 seconds.

4. While it's awake, the container saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes. Each wake restores the world before Paper starts.

This setup isn't free. The fixed cost is $25 to $30 a month:

- The $5 Workers Paid plan.
- A zone on the [Pro plan](https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/) or Business, because Spectrum doesn't work on Free zones. Pro is $25 a month, or $20 a month billed yearly.

On top of that, you pay for the container only while it's awake. With Cloudflare's [published rates](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/), a server played two hours a day adds about $5 a month, and one that never sleeps adds about $40 to $90.

## Get started

### What you need

- macOS or Linux with glibc. Windows and Alpine aren't supported.
- [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.4 or newer, [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.12 or newer, and [Docker](https://www.docker.com) running.
- A Cloudflare account on Workers Paid, with R2 enabled and a workers.dev subdomain set up. Alchemy keeps its deploy state in a Worker on that subdomain.
- A domain on Cloudflare whose zone is on the Pro or Business plan, or has Spectrum Enterprise. Free zones can't use Spectrum.
- To accept the [Minecraft EULA](https://www.minecraft.net/eula).

### Steps

1. Install the dependencies.

   ```sh
   bun install --frozen-lockfile
   ```

2. Connect your Cloudflare account. The project deploys with [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run), and this script signs it in.

   ```sh
   bun scripts/setup-alchemy.ts
   ```

   Select **OAuth** when asked how to sign in, keep **All Scopes**, then approve access in your browser. Basic Scopes can't create the Spectrum route. If you have more than one account, pick the one to deploy to.

3. Create a `.env` file. Use a hostname that has no DNS record yet.

   ```dotenv
   MINECRAFT_EULA=true
   MINECRAFT_SPECTRUM_HOST=play.example.com
   MINECRAFT_PLAYERS=Alice,Bob
   ```

4. Deploy. The script shows its changes and ask…

# Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations

This repository holds the paper *Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations* by L. Alpöge and
T. Buckmaster and the Lean 4 formalization that accompanies it.

## Contents

- `paper/finite-time-blow-up-navier-stokes.pdf`: the paper (79 pages, version of 20 November 2026).
- `lean/`: the Lean package (Lean v4.33.1 with Mathlib, at the revision pinned in `lean/lakefile.toml`).
  - `lean/README.md` explains how the formal statements relate to Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.2
    and Appendix B of the paper, and where the formal proofs differ from the proofs of the paper.
  - `lean/NOTICE` says in words what each statement file contains and what is proved.

## The Lean package

The statement files at the top of `lean/` give the definitions and state the theorems with `sorry` in
place of their proofs; `Solution.lean` proves them from the library `lean/Breakdown/`. Each
`comparator*.json` pairs a statement file with `Solution.lean`, names the theorems whose statements must agree,
and permits only the axioms `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice`.

To build, from `lean/`:

```bash
lake exe cache get
```

```bash
lake build
```

The library is large (about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines), and a full build needs a great deal of memory and
time.

## What is and is not here

The formalization contains no data. The certificate whose hash the paper gives is not in this repository; the
paper says that it will be released. That the certificate satisfies the conditions of Appendix B is verified by
a rigorous computation, involving interval arithmetic (128 bits of precision, with the Arb library through
FLINT), which is not part of the formalization and is not in this repository either.

The source of the paper is not in this repository.

## State of the Lean text

The package is the one of the paper's working repository, with one patch of 20 November 2026 applied to the
cell-layer statements and to the library proofs that depend on them: the weight of one bound becomes
$(|m|+\tfrac12)^2$ in place of $m^2+\tfrac14$, one constant of a cell may be zero, and the set of the harmonics
of the model in a cell is restricted to those that do not vanish there. Appendix B of the paper states the
conditions in this patched form. The patched package was not rebuilt when this repository was assembled.

# ARTEX **Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.** Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools, and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/BaaRai/ARTEX?label=release&color=6b34db)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](go.mod) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
--- ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets. - **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven. - **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two. - **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic; findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response. - **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates, token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output. - **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL, your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama. --- ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key) docker compose up -d --build # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL ``` Open **http://localhost:8787**. On the first visit `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup: ```bash docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token" ``` > Multi-arch release images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) are published to GitHub Container > Registry at `ghcr.io/baarai/artex` from the next tagged release; v0.7.0 predates the publish > step.
